name: Where Are You Storyboard
title: If God doesn't need anything, why did he make you?
message: God doesn't need us. He made us because he wanted us, and he still wanted us when we hid from him.

sections.1. The question: One question in the viewer's own words.
sections.2. The stakes: If he needs nothing, do we matter?
sections.3. The easy answers fail: Two common answers break against the verse.
sections.4. The turn: He chose to make us. Would he still want us?
sections.5. The story: The fruit, the hiding, and God calling out. His words are held back.
sections.6. The comeback: The cost is real, and he still takes care of them.
sections.7. The moment: The held-back words. This is the longest hold in the film.
sections.8. What it means: Only what the moment already showed.
sections.9. How it applies to us: One line, and the face from the garden becomes ours.
sections.10. The conclusion: The answer, then the opening picture again, now in gold.

shots.words: If God doesn't need anything,
shots.picture: The whole universe turning by itself: a galaxy, a sun, planets. The camera falls fast toward one small Earth.
shots.understand: All of this runs without us
shots.why: Start at the biggest scale so the next shot feels tiny
shots.acting: No people yet

shots.words: why did he make you?
shots.picture: One tiny person on a dark hill under a huge sky.
shots.why: This is the frame the whole film comes back to. Keep the size and position exact
shots.acting: The person lifts their head on 'you'

shots.words: The Bible says in Acts 17:25 that God doesn't need anything from us.
shots.picture: Sun, sea, mountains and birds, all moving without a single person. The verse card sits low in the frame.
shots.understand: This claim comes from the Bible
shots.why: The world running without us shows the verse before we explain it
shots.acting: Waves roll on 'God'. Birds cross on 'need'
shots.text: Acts 17:25: "nor is he served by human hands, as though he needed anything"

shots.words: But we all want to feel needed.
shots.picture: A small child's hand reaches up and takes an adult's hand.
shots.why: One plain human picture of being needed
shots.acting: The small hand closes on 'needed'

shots.words: So do we even matter to him?
shots.picture: Looking straight down at the same person, now alone, with their hands open.
shots.why: The high angle makes them small. The empty hands answer the child's hand before it
shots.acting: They open their hands on 'matter'

shots.words: Maybe he was lonely. But that would mean he needed us.
shots.picture: A chalk drawing of a table with one lamp and empty chairs, and the word LONELY? One chalk line strikes it out.
shots.why: Chalk marks this as an idea, so nobody mistakes it for something that happened
shots.acting: The word writes on 'lonely'. The line strikes on 'needed'

shots.words: Maybe he wanted our worship. He deserves it, but he doesn't need it.
shots.picture: A chalk crowd with raised hands under chalk stars, and the word WORSHIP? The line strikes it out.
shots.understand: He's worthy of it, and he still doesn't need it
shots.why: Pulling back shows how small the crowd is, without mocking it
shots.acting: Hands rise on 'worship'. Line strikes on 'need'

shots.words: So what's the real reason? Revelation 4:11 says he created everything because he chose to.
shots.picture: The chalk blows away. Gold light breaks out of the dark, and sea, land, trees and birds appear from it.
shots.understand: He made everything because he chose to
shots.why: First gold in the film, because this is the first time God acts
shots.acting: Each thing appears on 'created' and 'everything'
shots.text: Revelation 4:11: "by your will they existed and were created"

shots.words: But would he still want us if we turned against him?
shots.picture: The light settles into a garden. Two people walk together, and the shadow of a tree slides across them.
shots.why: The shadow says what's coming before the story starts
shots.acting: They walk easily. The shadow reaches them on 'turned'

shots.words: In Genesis, God told Adam and Eve not to eat from one tree.
shots.picture: From above, a full garden with one tree standing alone. Adam and Eve look at it.
shots.why: The viewer needs this fact, or the fruit means nothing
shots.acting: A gold ripple comes down on 'told'. They turn toward the tree on 'one'

shots.words: But the serpent tells Eve she'll "be like God" if she does.
shots.picture: Over the serpent's coils as it slides down a branch toward Eve. The fruit hangs between them.
shots.why: Seeing it from behind the serpent puts us too close
shots.acting: Its head stops by Eve on 'tells'. She looks up at the fruit on 'like'

shots.words: She eats the fruit.
shots.picture: Her hand brings the fruit up, and she bites. It isn't drawn as an apple, because Genesis doesn't name the fruit.
shots.why: The verb lands on its word, with nothing else in frame
shots.acting: Bite on 'eats'. Nothing moves after it

shots.words: She gives some to Adam, and he eats.
shots.picture: She holds it out. He takes it and eats.
shots.why: Keep both people in one frame so giving and eating stay linked
shots.acting: She reaches on 'gives'. He bites on 'eats'

shots.words: They realize they're naked, and they sew fig leaves together.
shots.picture: All the color drains out of the garden. Their hands stitch big fig leaves together.
shots.why: Stay on hands, so the shame reads without showing bodies
shots.acting: Color drains on 'realize'. Hands pull the thread on 'sew'

shots.words: Genesis 3:8 says they hear God walking in the garden, and they hide.
shots.picture: We never see God. Grass and leaves bend in a line moving toward them, with a gold edge. They run for the dark trees.
shots.understand: God is near, and the Bible says so
shots.why: The sound moves through the garden. This keeps Genesis 3:8 true without drawing God as a man
shots.acting: Their heads turn on 'walking'. They run on 'hide'
shots.text: Genesis 3:8: "And they heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden"

shots.words: Hebrews 4:13 says no one is hidden from God.
shots.picture: From high above the trees. Through one gap, the two of them are plainly visible.
shots.why: The view from above answers the hiding. We'll use this frame again
shots.acting: They press themselves down on 'hidden'
shots.text: Hebrews 4:13: "And no creature is hidden from his sight"

shots.words: God doesn't need them. He could just leave them there.
shots.picture: In the dark trees. The two of them crouch without moving. The moving leaves have stopped.
shots.why: The one planned stillness before the call
shots.acting: Nothing moves. Her hand tightens on his arm on 'leave'

shots.words: But he calls out to them. We'll come back to what he said.
shots.picture: A gold ripple moves through the trees and reaches them. Their heads lift. Then the whole frame freezes.
shots.understand: He called. What did he say?
shots.why: We hold back his words so they land at the end. The freeze keeps the question open
shots.acting: Heads lift on 'calls'. Everything freezes on 'We'll'

shots.words: There are consequences. They will die,
shots.picture: A dried fig leaf. Dust falls through an open hand.
shots.why: Dust comes from Genesis 3:19. It shows death with no violence
shots.acting: The hand opens on 'die'

shots.words: and God sends them out of the garden.
shots.picture: The edge of the green garden and dry land beyond it. Two small people walk toward the dry land. No gate.
shots.why: Show how much is behind them
shots.acting: They stop just short of the dry land on 'garden'

shots.words: But before they leave, Genesis 3:21 says God makes them clothes.
shots.picture: Gold ripples settle over them. The fig leaves fall away, and clothes of skin rest on their shoulders.
shots.understand: He is still caring for them
shots.why: Gold returns because the text says God did this
shots.acting: They look up on 'before'. The leaves fall on 'makes'
shots.text: Genesis 3:21: "And the LORD God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skins and clothed them."

shots.words: They turned against him, and he's still taking care of them.
shots.picture: Eve's fingers touch the clothing. She looks up. The verse card stays until she does.
shots.why: Let the viewer feel it on a face
shots.acting: Her fingers touch the cloth on 'turned'. She looks up on 'still'

shots.words: And he never stopped. John 3:16 says, "For God so loved the world,
shots.picture: We rise above the land and time passes across the Earth. One gold point appears on the planet.
shots.understand: It didn't end in the garden
shots.why: This links the garden to Jesus
shots.acting: Sun and moon race on 'never stopped'. The point lights on 'loved'
shots.text: John 3:16: "For God so loved the world,"

shots.words: that he gave his only Son."
shots.picture: A far-off hill. One cross in gold light, with Jesus lit and in color. No blood, and no closeness.
shots.why: Stay far away and hold. The verse does the work
shots.acting: Stillness. The light grows on 'Son'

shots.words: Here's what he said.
shots.picture: Back to the frozen frame in the dark trees. The music cuts out, and the gold ripple starts moving again.
shots.understand: This is what we were waiting for
shots.why: The freeze from shot 18 pays off
shots.acting: The freeze lets go on 'said'

shots.words: God's first words to them aren't "How could you?"
shots.picture: Adam's face in the leaves. His eyes are shut tight. He's braced for it.
shots.why: We feel what he expects to hear
shots.acting: He flinches on 'How'

shots.words: They're "Where are you?"
shots.picture: The whole dark garden, huge. Two tiny people. One thin gold line reaches them. The words fill the sky.
shots.why: The longest hold in the film. Silence after the words, with one small change inside it
shots.acting: His eyes open on 'Where'. The gold line reaches them during the silence

shots.words: He already knew where they were.
shots.picture: The same view from above as shot 16, now with a gold ring around them.
shots.why: Same frame, new meaning. Nothing new is introduced
shots.acting: The ring closes on 'knew'

shots.words: He didn't need an answer. He wanted them.
shots.picture: Both faces lift into warm gold light.
shots.understand: Need and want. This is the whole film
shots.why: The film's one idea lands on their faces
shots.acting: Eyes open on 'answer'. The light reaches them on 'wanted'

shots.words: So when we fail, we don't have to hide from him.
shots.picture: Match cut: Adam's face becomes the face of the person from the opening, in the same spot in the frame, alone in a dim room. They lower their hands and look toward the window.
shots.why: The face stays in the same spot through the cut, which ties the garden to our lives with no new idea
shots.acting: Hands lower on 'hide'. They turn to the light on 'him'

shots.words: He didn't make us because he needed us.
shots.picture: The camera pulls back out to the universe from shot 1, turning on its own.
shots.why: Shot 1 in reverse
shots.acting: No people

shots.words: He made us because he wanted us.
shots.picture: We come back down to the Earth at night, covered in warm lights.
shots.why: The same scale as the last shot, but now it's full of people
shots.acting: Lights come on across the Earth from 'wanted'

shots.words: If he still wanted Adam and Eve after all that,
shots.picture: Sunrise on the dry land. Adam and Eve walk on in their clothes, with gold light on their shoulders.
shots.why: Their last picture is a warm one
shots.acting: She turns her head to the sun on 'still'

shots.words: why would he ever stop wanting you?
shots.picture: The opening picture: the same person on the same hill under the same stars. Now they're in gold light, hands open.
shots.why: The final image is the answer, in the exact frame of shot 2
shots.acting: They open their hands on 'you'
shots.text: FOURTH WATCH logo after the last word
